meaning_en: to run over; to run (a red light)
definition_de: mit einem Fahrzeug über ein Tier oder einen Menschen fahren; auch: eine rote Ampel / ein Stoppschild überfahren (nicht anhalten). Trennbar (über|fahren, fährt über, ist übergefahren) heißt es selten 'mit der Fähre ans andere Ufer fahren'.
example_de: Der Fahrer bremste scharf, sonst hätte er die Enten auf der Straße überfahren.
example_en: The driver braked hard, otherwise he would have run over the ducks on the road.
visual_idea: Collocation 'ein Tier überfahren', shown as a near miss: a car stopped just centimetres before a mother duck and her ducklings crossing the road. Clear, emotional and funny instead of gory; the Konjunktiv 'hätte … überfahren' shows the inseparable participle without ge-. 'Eine rote Ampel überfahren' was the second candidate but reads as 'über die Straße fahren'.
image_prompt: a small car has stopped abruptly on a quiet village road, its front bumper only a few centimetres from a mother duck leading six fluffy ducklings across the asphalt in a line, the driver behind the windshield with wide eyes and both hands gripping the wheel, low angle at road level next to the ducks, green fields and a farmhouse behind
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: on a quiet village road a mother duck leads her ducklings across the asphalt; a small car drives toward them and brakes hard, stopping just centimetres before the ducks, which calmly keep waddling across while the shocked driver exhales; static low camera at road level
